grammar.title: Giving to someone with 把...V给
grammar.pattern: 主语 + 把 + 宾语 + 动词 + 给 + 对象
grammar.explanation: Adding 给 (gěi) after the verb in a 把 sentence shows the object ends up with someone — "do X to it and give it to someone". It's common with verbs like 送, 还, 卖, 发 that involve handing something over.

grammar.title: Potential complement: V + 得/不 + 了
grammar.explanation: 得 or 不 between a verb and 了 asks or states whether an action is possible to complete — "can/can't manage to do something". 得了 (de liǎo) means it's possible, and 不了 (bu liǎo) means it isn't, often because of a physical or practical limit.

sentences.zh: 为了身体健康，他常常运动。
sentences.pinyin: Wèile shēntǐ jiànkāng, tā chángcháng yùndòng.
sentences.en: For the sake of his health, he often exercises.

sentences.zh: 为了学汉语，她常常听中文歌。
sentences.pinyin: Wèile xué Hànyǔ, tā chángcháng tīng Zhōngwén gē.
sentences.en: In order to learn Chinese, she often listens to Chinese songs.

sentences.zh: 为了买房子，他们努力工作。
sentences.pinyin: Wèile mǎi fángzi, tāmen nǔlì gōngzuò.
sentences.en: In order to buy a house, they work hard.

sentences.zh: 我只是问问，没有别的意思。
sentences.pinyin: Wǒ zhǐshì wènwen, méiyǒu bié de yìsi.
sentences.en: I'm just asking, nothing else meant by it.
He just wants to help you.

sentences.zh: 这张桌子坐不下六个人。
sentences.pinyin: Zhè zhāng zhuōzi zuò bu xià liù gè rén.
sentences.en: This table can't seat six people.
